newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close higher, CAC-40 above 2,600.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close higher, CAC-40 above 2,600.

text.p: French shares closed sharply higher on Tuesday with a 1.55 percent gain as the blue-chip index moved back into the 2,600 territory, fuelled by a Monday gain on Wall Street and a solid dollar, dealers said.
But the Paris market closed below the day's high of 2,617.56 -- well below the February 18 all-time record of 2,658.62 -- when Wall Street turned initial Tuesday gains into losses.
Investors are awaiting Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress starting on Wednesday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed was up 39.87 points or 1.55 percent at 2,607.72.
* February futures closed at 2,608 against 2,570 on Monday.
* Volume was 8.7 billion francs, of which six billion on CAC-40 shares.
* Valeo closed 1.53 percent lower at 380.40 francs before reporting a rise in its 1996 net attributable profit to 1.2 billion francs from 1.01 billion.
* AGF closed 1.88 percent higher at 222 francs, giving up much of earlier rise on rumours Germany's Allianz could make a bid. Allianz had no comment.
* AXA closed at 383.10, up 1.35 percent but below a historic high of 383.40 reached earlier on the day.

A company spokesman declined to comment on rumours AXA could sell its British subsidiary Equity and Law. A company official did tell a news conference on the Equity and Law results that Axa was "at ease" with analysts' forecasts of a net attributable profit of between 3.6 and 3.9 billion francs against 2.73 billion in 1995.
Axa and UAP are set to announce their results on March 26.
* Sanofi closed 3.06 percent lower at 538 francs after reporting slightly lower than expected 1996 net profits, up 11 percent on the previous year.
* Elf up 0.56 percent at 542. Results due tomorrow.
* Eridania, up 3.04 percent at 916 francs, benefits from its status of single listed French sugar stock following a planned Worms/Saint Louis tie-up.
* Eramet rises 7.41 percent to 290 francs after 11 percent fall on Monday when the government announced it planned to withdraw a mining licence in New Caledonia.
* Club Med adds another 4.64 percent to 451 francs, after Monday's 20 percent rise, following nomination of Euro Disney's Philippe Bourguignon as chairman.

* Total, up 2.98 percent at 456.70 francs, said it had not received an offer for an acquisition or merger concerning Total Petroleum North America Ltd (TOPNA) TPN, in which it has a 54.9 percent stake. But spokesman said company was willing to study an offer which would give the company a minority stake in a bigger North American refining group.
The Wall Street Journal said Ultramar Diamond Shamrock was in talks to buy TOPNA for $803 million.
* Navigation Mixte, controlled by Paribas, was suspended at 920 francs at midday, pending a statement.
